Automotive Tyres, Tubes and Rims Sectional Committee, TED 7

FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Automotive Tyres, Tubes and Rims Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport Engineering Division Council. In the formulation of this standard, considerable assistance has been derived from the following International Standards: ISO 14690 : 2004 -- Tubeless tyres -- Valves and components -- Test methods ETRTO -- Engineering Design Information -- 2008 -- Testing Methods -- Method for testing snap-in tubeless tyre valves For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS 15945 : 2011

Indian Standard TUBELESS TYRES -- VALVES AND COMPONENTS -- TEST METHODS
1 SCOPE This standard specifies test methods and performance requirements for snap-in tubeless tyre valves and their components, intended for, but not limited to, highway applications. 2 REFERENCE The following standard contains provision which through reference in this text, constitutes provision of this standard. At the time of publication, the edition indicated was valid. All standards are subject to revision and parties to agreements based on this standard is encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent edition of the standard indicated below: IS No. 10694 (Part1) : 1993/ISO 3911 : 1977 Title Automotive vehicles -- Rims -- General requirements: Part 1 Nomenclature, designation, marking and measurement (first revision) on the housing, and without flow cracks, blisters, voids, or other moulding defects; its mould parting line flash shall not exceed 1.3 mm in height or 0.15 mm in thickness at the outer edge. 4.2 Test Fixtures 4.2.1 Break both edges on both sides of the valvehole, to form either a 45� chamfer of 0.3 mm to 0.4 mm or such that they are rounded with a radius of 0.3 mm to 0.4 mm. Emery cloth or suitable tooling shall be used for this purpose. It is also recommended that the material of the test fixture shall be representative of the material of the actual rim.
NOTE -- The primary external seal of a snap-in valve in a valve hole is obtained from the rubber compression of the valve body onto the internal surface of the valve hole. Secondary external sealing can be present by the contact of the remainder of the valve body exterior to the surface of the material around the valve hole. Either or both of these seals may be affected by the compound curvatures in the wheel rims and by stock thickness.

4.2.2 The dimensions of the test fixtures shall be in accordance with Table 1. 4.3 Installation 4.3.1 All valves, wetted with clean water as a lubricant, shall be installed in a test fixture in accordance with 4.2 by applying a valve insertion force to the end of the valve metal insert or a valve traction force to the mouth of the valve, perpendicular to the plane of the valve mounting hole and directly through the centre of the valve mounting hole. However, no valve assembly shall be tested which has got damage resulting from installation. 4.3.2 A valve shall be considered properly seated when the entire indicator ring is observed to be through the rim or valve mounting hole fixture. 4.3.3 After installation, valve assemblies shall be thoroughly dried in the seating area before continuing testing. 5 TEST METHODS AND PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS 5.1 Adhesion 5.1.1 Test Procedure a) 1 Make two axial and parallel cuts, 180� apart,

3 TERMS AND DEFINITIONS For the purposes of this standard the definitions given in IS 10694 (Part 1) and the following shall apply. 3.1 Snap-in Valve -- Tyre valve having a rigid housing adhered to a resilient body designed to retain and seal the valve in the rim hole. 3.2 Unused Valve -- Snap-in valve that has completed final manufacturing processing at least 24 h previously, which has not been subjected to any test or service and which has been stored for no longer than 4 months in the dark at ambient temperature, in an optimal and non-aggressive environment.
NOTE -- Rubber compounds can change characteristics during their life expectancy.

3.3 Aged Valve -- Unused valve that has been subjected to 100 � 3�C for a minimum of 4 h in circulating hot air and cooled at 20�C to 26�C for a minimum of 4 h. 4 TEST SET-UP 4.1 Test Valve Description A snap-in valve unit free of rubber in the air passage, having no rubber or cement above the second thread

1) For a cup gasket seal, apply a pressure of 35 kPa; and 2) For a barrel seal, apply a pressure of 475 kPa. 5.2.2.2 Performance requirement Leakage shall be at a rate less than 0.2 cm3 /min. Alternatively, no bubble shall be detached during the test time of 1 min. 5.2.3 Low Temperature Test 5.2.3.1 Test Procedure Depress and release the valve core pin once after a 24 h minimum exposure at �40 � 3�C. Maintain assembly pressure at 180 � 15 kPa (see Fig. 1). b) Check for leakage with ethanol or methanol at �40 � 3�C, 25 mm above the valve mouth, with the assembly still pressurized to 180 kPa. c) Begin leak detection after a 1 min soak period. 5.2.3.2 Performance requirement Leakage shall be at a rate less than 0.2 cm3 /min. Alternatively, no bubble shall be detached during the test time of 1 min. 5.2.4 High Temperature Test 5.2.4.1 Test procedure a) Depress and release the valve core pin once after 48 h minimum soak period at 100 � 3�C. Maintain assembly pressure at 600 � 15 kPa (see Fig. 1). b) Check for leakage with 66 � 3�C clean water at not more than 50 mm above the valve mouth, with the assembly still pressurized to 600 kPa. a)

Alternatively, no bubble shall be detached during the test time of 1 min. 5.3 Valve Cap Seal -- Room Temperature Test (Optional, for Sealing Caps Only) 5.3.1 Test Procedure Screw the cap with a sealing gasket at 0.15 N�m to 0.20 N�m torque on a valve without a core. b) Immerse the valve assembly vertically in clean water at 23 � 5�C not more than 100 mm below the surface of the water (see Fig. 1). c) Check for leakage using a 475 kPa test pressure. 5.3.2 Performance Requirement Leakage shall be at rate less than 0.2 cm�/min. Alternatively, no bubble shall be detached during the test time of 1 min. 5.4 Valve-to-Rim Seal 5.4.1 Principal Temperature tests are performed to subject the test valve to extremes in temperature. The flexing of the valve simulates possible operational conditions. 3 a)

The same valve and assembly, as shown in Fig. 2, may be used for both tests, provided the low temperature test is conducted first. 5.4.2 Low Temperature Test 5.4.2.1 Test hole diameter and plate thickness Test hole diameter and plate thickness shall be as specified in Table 1. 5.4.2.2 Test procedure Mount the test valve on a test plate in accordance with 4.2 and 4.3. b) Expose the assembly to a temperature of 40 � 3�C for 24 h minimum to ensure the valve seal area is at the test temperature, while applying a test pressure of 180 � 15 kPa. c) Immerse the valve assembly, still pressurized to 180 � 15 kPa, with the valve mouth upwards, in ethanol or methanol at �40 � 3�C, and with the valve button not more than 100 mm below the surface of the liquid (see Fig. 1). d) Flex the immersed valve to an angle of 25 � 3� with respect to the axis of the valve mounting hole. Revolve the cap end of the valve one complete turn around the axis of the mounting hole, executing this single revolution at a uniform rate, without the application of torque to the valve body and within 15 s to 45 s. a)

IS 15945 : 2011 e) f) Place the assembly in a refrigerator at �40 � 3�C. Maintain the pressure at 180 � 15 kPa. Repeat steps (c) to (e) of the procedure at minimum intervals of 0.5 h a total of five times. diameter of 15.7 mm rim hole; and 2) 450 � 15 kPa air pressure for products suitable for diameter of 8.8 mm rim hole. c) Immerse the valve assembly, still pressurized to: 1) 600 � 15 kPa air pressure for products suitable for diameter of 11.3 mm and diameter of 15.7 mm rim hole; and 2) 450 � 15 kPa air pressure for products suitable for diameter of 8.8 mm rim hole. with the valve mouth upwards, in clean water at 66 � 3 �C, and with the valve button not more than 100 mm below the surface of the liquid (see Fig. 2). d) Flex the immersed valve to an angle of 25� � 3� with respect to the axis of the valve mounting hole. 5.4.2.3 Performance requirement Leakage shall be at a rate less than 0.2 cm�/min. Alternatively, no bubble shall be detached during the test time of 1 min at the rim seal before, during or after revolving and flexing the valve.
NOTE -- Air inclusions during installation are not considered.

Repeat steps (c) to (e) at minimum intervals of 0.5 h a total of five times; the last time shall be at the end of 72 h. 5.6 Burst 5.6.1 Test Hole Diameter and Plate Thickness Test hole diameter and plate thickness shall be as specified in Table 1. 5.6.2 Test Procedure a) Mount the valve on a test plate in accordance with 4.2 and 4.3. b) Apply hydrostatic pressure to the valve base to attain a pressure of 1.4 MPa within a 1 min interval. c) Maintain this maximum pressure for an additional 2 min. d) The test shall be conducted at 20�C to 26 �C.

f)

5.4.3.3 Performance requirement Leakage shall be at a rate less than 0.2 cm�/min. Alternatively, no bubble shall be detached during the test time of 1 min at the rim seal before, during or after revolving and flexing the valve.
NOTE -- Air inclusions during installation are not considered.

5.5 Installation Tests 5.5.1 Force to Seat 5.5.1.1 Test hole diameter and plate thickness Test hole diameter and plate thickness shall be as specified in Table 1. 5.5.1.2 Test procedure Mount the valve on a test plate in accordance with 4.2 and 4.3 at a rate of 150 � 15 mm/min, while measuring the force needed to seat the valve using an appropriate force measuring method. 5.5.1.3 Performance requirements The force to seat the valve shall be between, for diameter of 8.8 mm hole, 180 N and 400 N; and b) for diameter of 11.3 mm and diameter of 15.7 mm hole, 180 N and 450 N. There shall be no tearing or rupturing of the valve. 5.5.2 Force to Pull Out 5.5.2.1 Test hole diameter and plate thickness Test hole diameter and plate thickness shall be as specified in Table 1. 5.5.2.2 Test procedure a) Install the valve according to 5.5.1.2; and b) Apply and measure the additional force needed to break or pull out the valve. 5.5.2.3 Performance Requirement The minimum force to break the valve base or pull the valve out of the hole shall be, a) for diameter of 8.8 mm hole, 480 N; and b) for diameter of 11.3 mm and diameter of 15.7 mm hole, 560 N. 5 a)

5.6.3 Performance Requirement The valve shall not burst. 5.7 Ozone Resistance 5.7.1 Test Hole Diameter and Plate Thickness Test hole diameter and plate thickness shall be as specified in Table 1. 5.7.2 Test Procedure Age an unmounted valve for 72 h at 100 � 3�C. b) Mount the aged valve on a test plate in accordance with 4.2 and 4.3. c) Deflect the valve 10� from its axis with respect to the axis of the mounting hole and retain it in that position for the duration of the test. d) Place the valve in a darkened enclosure at 20�C to 26�C for a minimum of 24 h. e) Place the valve in an ozone circulating chamber, with 100 � 5 parts of ozone to 100 million parts of air, for 72 h at 38 � 3�C 5.7.3 Performance Requirement The valve rubber shall not exhibit any cracks when viewed at 5X amplification. 5.8 Flexing Resistance 5.8.1 Test Hole Diameter and Plate Thickness Test hole diameter and plate thickness shall be as specified in Table 1. 5.8.2 Test Procedure This procedure involves flexing a valve to simulate possible operational conditions. a) Mount the test valve on a test plate in accordance with 4.2 and 4.3 (see Fig. 3); and b) Flex the valve at a flexing angle of � 25� from a)

IS 15945 : 2011 the valve axis, at a frequency of 2 Hz and with a tolerance of � 1� while maintaining a pressure of 200 kPa to the valve assembly (see Fig. 3). 5.8.3 Performance Requirement There shall be no failure after 40 000 cycles. Failure is defined as a crack visible to the naked eye.
